Main.sentence: Calvin Coolidge (born John Calvin Coolidge Jr. ;  /ˈkuːlɪdʒ/ ___E:KOOL-ij U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)___ ; July 4, 1872 – January 5, 1933) was the 30th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , serving from 1923 to 1929. A ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ lawyer from ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ , he previously served as the 29th ___E:vice president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States)___ from 1921 to 1923, under President ___E:Warren G. Harding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_G._Harding)___ , and as the 48th ___E:governor of Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Massachusetts)___ from 1919 to 1921. Coolidge gained a reputation as a ___E:small-government conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_conservatism)___ , with a taciturn personality and dry sense of humor that earned him the nickname " Silent Cal ".
Coolidge began his career as a member of the ___E:Massachusetts State House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_House_of_Representatives)___ .
He rose up the ranks of Massachusetts politics and was ___E:elected governor in 1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1918_Massachusetts_gubernatorial_election)___ .

As governor, Coolidge ran on the record of ___E:fiscal conservatism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_conservatism)___ , strong support for ___E:women's suffrage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage)___ , and vague opposition to ___E:Prohibition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States)___ .

His prompt and effective response to the ___E:Boston police strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_police_strike)___ of 1919 thrust him into the national spotlight as a man of decisive action.

The following year, the Republican Party nominated Coolidge as the running mate to Senator Warren G. Harding in the ___E:1920 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_United_States_presidential_election)___ , which they won in a ___E:landslide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide_victory)___ .
Coolidge served as vice president until Harding's death in 1923, after which he assumed the presidency.

During his presidency, Coolidge restored public confidence in the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ after the ___E:Harding administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harding_administration)___ 's many ___E:scandals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_G._Harding#Scandals)___ .

He signed into law the ___E:Indian Citizenship Act of 1924 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Citizenship_Act_of_1924)___ , which granted ___E:U.S. citizenship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._citizenship)___ to all Native Americans, and oversaw a period of rapid and expansive economic growth known as the " ___E:Roaring Twenties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roaring_Twenties)___ ", leaving office with considerable popularity.

Coolidge was known for his hands-off governing approach and pro-business stance; biographer ___E:Claude Fuess U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Fuess)___ wrote: "He embodied the spirit and hopes of the middle class, could interpret their longings and express their opinions.

That he did represent the genius of the average is the most convincing proof of his strength."  Coolidge ___E:chose not to run U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_do_not_choose_to_run)___ again in ___E:1928 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_United_States_presidential_election)___ , remarking that ten years as president would be "longer than any other man has had it—too long!" [b]

Coolidge is widely admired for his stalwart support of ___E:racial equality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_equality)___ during a period of heightened racial tension,  and is highly regarded by advocates of smaller government and laissez-faire economics; supporters of an active central government generally view him far less favorably.

His critics argue that he failed to use the country's economic boom to help struggling farmers and workers in other flailing industries,  and there is still ___E:much debate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causes_of_the_Great_Depression#Calvin_Coolidge_(1923–29))___ among historians about the extent to which Coolidge's economic policies contributed to the onset of the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , which began shortly after he left office.
Scholars ___E:have ranked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States#Scholar_survey_summary)___ Coolidge in the lower half of U.S. presidents.

John Calvin Coolidge Jr. was born on July 4, 1872, in ___E:Plymouth Notch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth,_Vermont)___ , Vermont—the only U.S. president to be born on ___E:Independence Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States))___ .

He was the elder of the two children of ___E:John Calvin Coolidge Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Calvin_Coolidge_Sr.)___ and Victoria Josephine Moor. Although named for his father, from early childhood Coolidge was addressed by his middle name. The name Calvin was used in multiple generations of the Coolidge family, apparently selected in honor of ___E:John Calvin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Calvin)___ , the ___E:Protestant Reformer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Reformer)___ , with Coolidge describing his ancestors as "English Puritan stock" in his Autobiography.

Coolidge's earliest American ancestor, John Coolidge, emigrated from ___E:Cottenham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottenham)___ , Cambridgeshire, England, around 1630 and settled in ___E:Watertown, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertown,_Massachusetts)___ .

Coolidge also descended from ___E:Samuel Appleton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Appleton_(born_1625))___ , who settled in ___E:Ipswich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich,_Massachusetts)___ and led the ___E:Massachusetts Bay Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Bay_Colony)___ during ___E:King Philip's War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Philip%27s_War)___ .

Coolidge's great-great-grandfather, another John Coolidge, was an American military officer in the ___E:Revolutionary War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War)___ and one of the first ___E:selectmen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Selectmen)___ of the town of Plymouth.
His grandfather ___E:Calvin Galusha Coolidge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Galusha_Coolidge)___ served in the Vermont House of Representatives.

His cousin ___E:Park Pollard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Pollard)___ was a businessman in ___E:Cavendish, Vermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavendish,_Vermont)___ , and the longtime chair of the Vermont Democratic Party.
Coolidge's mother was the daughter of Hiram Dunlap Moor, a Plymouth Notch farmer, and Abigail Franklin.
Coolidge Senior engaged in many occupations and developed a statewide reputation as a prosperous farmer, storekeeper, and public servant.

He held various local offices, including ___E:justice of the peace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_of_the_peace)___ and tax collector and served in both houses of the ___E:Vermont General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont_General_Assembly)___ .
When Coolidge was 12 years old, his chronically ill mother died at the age of 39, perhaps from ___E:tuberculosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis)___ .

His younger sister, Abigail Grace Coolidge (1875–1890), died at the age of 15, probably of appendicitis, when Coolidge was 18. Coolidge's father married a Plymouth schoolteacher in 1891, and lived to the age of 80.

Coolidge attended the ___E:Black River Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_River_Academy)___ and then ___E:St. Johnsbury Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Johnsbury_Academy)___ before enrolling at ___E:Amherst College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amherst_College)___ , where he distinguished himself in the debating class.
As a senior, he joined the ___E:Phi Gamma Delta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Gamma_Delta)___ fraternity and graduated cum laude .

While at Amherst, Coolidge was profoundly influenced by philosophy professor ___E:Charles Edward Garman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Edward_Garman)___ , a ___E:Congregational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregationalism_in_the_United_States)___ mystic who had a ___E:neo-Hegelian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Hegelianism)___ philosophy.

Coolidge explained Garman's ethics forty years later: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}

[T]here is a standard of righteousness that might does not make right, that the end does not justify the means, and that expediency as a working principle is bound to fail. The only hope of perfecting human relationships is in accordance with the law of service under which men are not so solicitous about what they shall get as they are about what they shall give. Yet people are entitled to the rewards of their industry.
What they earn is theirs, no matter how small or how great.
But the possession of property carries the obligation to use it in a larger service...
At his father's urging after graduation, Coolidge moved to ___E:Northampton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton,_Massachusetts)___ , to become a lawyer.

Coolidge followed the common practice of apprenticing with a local law firm, Hammond & Field, and ___E:reading law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_law)___ with them. ___E:John C. Hammond U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C_Hammond)___ and Henry P. Field, both Amherst graduates, introduced Coolidge to practicing law in the county seat of ___E:Hampshire County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampshire_County,_Massachusetts)___ .

In 1897, Coolidge was admitted to the ___E:Massachusetts bar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Bar_Association)___ , becoming a ___E:country lawyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_lawyer)___ .

With his savings and a small inheritance from his grandfather, Coolidge opened his own law office in Northampton in 1898. He practiced commercial law, believing that he served his clients best by staying out of court.
As his reputation as a hard-working and diligent attorney grew, local banks and other businesses began to retain his services.

In 1903, Coolidge met ___E:Grace Goodhue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Goodhue)___ , a graduate of the ___E:University of Vermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Vermont)___ and a teacher at Northampton's ___E:Clarke School for the Deaf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarke_School_for_the_Deaf)___ .
They married on October 4, 1905, at 2:30 p.m. in a small ceremony which took place in the parlor of Grace's family's house, having overcome her mother's objections to the marriage.

The newlyweds went on a ___E:honeymoon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeymoon)___ trip to ___E:Montreal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal)___ , originally planned for two weeks but cut short by a week at Coolidge's request.
After 25 years he wrote of Grace, "for almost a quarter of a century she has borne with my infirmities and I have rejoiced in her graces".
The Coolidges had two sons: ___E:John U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Coolidge)___ (1906–2000) and Calvin Jr. (1908–1924).

On June 30, 1924, Calvin Jr. played ___E:tennis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis)___ with his brother on the White House tennis courts without putting on socks and developed a ___E:blister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blister)___ on one of his toes. The blister subsequently degenerated into ___E:sepsis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepsis)___ .
He died a little over a week later at the age of 16.
Coolidge never forgave himself for Calvin Jr's death.

His elder son John said it "hurt [Coolidge] terribly", and psychiatric biographer Robert E. Gilbert, author of The Tormented President: Calvin Coolidge, Death, and Clinical Depression , said that Coolidge "ceased to function as President after the death of his sixteen-year-old son".

Gilbert writes that after Calvin Jr.'s death Coolidge displayed all ten of the symptoms the ___E:American Psychiatric Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Psychiatric_Association)___ lists as evidence of ___E:major depressive disorder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder)___ .

John later became a railroad executive, helped start the Coolidge Foundation, and was instrumental in creating the ___E:President Calvin Coolidge State Historic Site U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Calvin_Coolidge_State_Historic_Site)___ .
Coolidge was frugal, and when it came to securing a home, he insisted upon renting.
He and his wife attended Northampton's Edwards ___E:Congregational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregational_church)___ Church before and after his presidency.

The ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Republican_Party_(United_States))___ was dominant in New England at the time, and Coolidge followed the example of Hammond and Field by becoming active in local politics.

In 1896, Coolidge campaigned for Republican presidential candidate ___E:William McKinley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley)___ , and was selected to be a member of the Republican City Committee the next year.  In 1898, he won election to the ___E:City Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Council)___ of Northampton, placing second in a ward where the top three candidates were elected.
The position offered no salary but provided Coolidge with valuable political experience.
In 1899, the city council made Coolidge city solicitor.
He was elected to a one-year term in 1900 and reelected in 1901.  This position gave Coolidge more experience as a lawyer and paid a salary of $600 (equivalent to $22,678 in 2024).
In 1902, the city council selected a Democrat for city solicitor, and Coolidge returned to private practice.

Soon thereafter, the ___E:clerk of courts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_clerk)___ for the county died, and Coolidge was chosen to replace him. The position paid well, but it barred him from practicing law, so he remained at the job for only a year.
In 1904, Coolidge suffered his sole defeat at the ballot box, losing an election to the Northampton ___E:school board U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Education)___ .
When told that some of his neighbors voted against him because he had no children in the schools he would govern, the recently married Coolidge replied, "Might give me time!"

In 1906, the local Republican committee nominated Coolidge for election to the ___E:Massachusetts House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_House_of_Representatives)___ .

He won a close victory over the incumbent Democrat, and reported to ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ for the 1907 session of the ___E:Massachusetts General Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_General_Court)___ .

In his freshman term, Coolidge served on minor committees and, although he usually voted with the party, was known as a ___E:Progressive Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Party_(United_States,_1912))___ , voting in favor of such measures as ___E:women's suffrage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage)___ and the ___E:direct election of Senators U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ .
While in Boston, Coolidge became an ally, and then a liegeman, of then U.S.

Senator ___E:Winthrop Murray Crane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winthrop_Murray_Crane)___ , who controlled the Massachusetts Republican Party's western faction; Crane's party rival in eastern Massachusetts was U.S.
Senator ___E:Henry Cabot Lodge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cabot_Lodge)___ .

Coolidge forged another key strategic alliance with ___E:Guy Currier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Currier)___ , who had served in both state houses and had the social distinction, wealth, personal charm, and broad circle of friends Coolidge lacked, and which had a lasting impact on his political career.
In 1907, Coolidge was reelected.
In the 1908 session he was more outspoken, though not in a leadership position.

Instead of vying for another term in the ___E:State House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_State_House)___ , Coolidge returned home to his growing family and ran for mayor of Northampton when the incumbent Democrat retired.

He was well liked in the town, and defeated his challenger by a vote of 1,597 to 1,409.  During his first term from 1910 to 1911, he increased teachers' salaries and retired some of the city's debt while still managing to effect a slight tax decrease.
In 1911, he was renominated and defeated the same opponent by a slightly larger margin.

In 1911, the ___E:State Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Senate)___ for the Hampshire County area retired and successfully encouraged Coolidge to run for his seat for the 1912 session.
Coolidge defeated his Democratic opponent by a large margin.

At the start of that term, he became chairman of a committee to arbitrate the " ___E:Bread and Roses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_and_Roses)___ " strike by the workers of the ___E:American Woolen Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Woolen_Company)___ in ___E:Lawrence, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Massachusetts)___ . [c] After two tense months, the company agreed to the workers' demands, in a settlement proposed by the committee.

A major issue affecting Massachusetts Republicans in 1912 was ___E:the party split U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_United_States_presidential_election)___ between the progressive wing, which favored ___E:Theodore Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt)___ , and the conservative wing, which favored ___E:William Howard Taft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft)___ .
Although he favored some progressive measures, Coolidge refused to leave the Republican party.

When the new ___E:Progressive Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Party_(United_States,_1912))___ declined to run a candidate in his state senate district, Coolidge won reelection against his Democratic opponent by an increased margin.

In the 1913 session, Coolidge enjoyed renowned success in arduously navigating to passage the Western Trolley Act, which connected Northampton with a dozen similar industrial communities in ___E:Western Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Massachusetts)___ .

Coolidge intended to retire after his second term, as was customary, but when the ___E:president of the state senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Massachusetts_Senate)___ , ___E:Levi H. Greenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_H._Greenwood)___ , considered running for lieutenant governor, Coolidge decided to run for the Senate again in hopes of being elected its presiding officer.
Greenwood later decided to run for reelection to the Senate, and was defeated primarily due to his opposition to women's suffrage.
Coolidge was in favor of the women's vote, and was reelected.
With Crane's help, Coolidge assumed the presidency of a closely divided Senate.
After his election in January 1914, Coolidge delivered a published and frequently quoted speech, Have Faith in Massachusetts , which summarized his philosophy of government.
Coolidge's speech was well received, and he attracted some admirers on its account.
Towards the end of the term, many of them were proposing Coolidge's name for nomination to lieutenant governor.
After winning reelection to the Senate by an increased margin in the 1914 elections, Coolidge was reelected unanimously to be President of the Senate.
Coolidge's supporters, led by fellow Amherst alumnus ___E:Frank Stearns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Stearns)___ , encouraged him again to run for lieutenant governor.
Stearns, an executive with the Boston department store R. H.
Stearns, became another key ally, and began a publicity campaign on Coolidge's behalf before he announced his candidacy at the end of the 1915 legislative session.

Coolidge entered the ___E:primary election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ for lieutenant governor and was nominated to run alongside gubernatorial candidate ___E:Samuel W. McCall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_W._McCall)___ .

Coolidge was the leading vote-getter in the Republican primary, and ___E:balanced U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticket_balance)___ the Republican ticket by adding a western presence to McCall's eastern base of support.
McCall and Coolidge won the 1915 election to their respective one-year terms, with Coolidge defeating his opponent by more than 50,000 votes.

In Massachusetts, the lieutenant governor does not preside over the state Senate, as is the case in many other states; nevertheless, as lieutenant governor, Coolidge was a deputy governor functioning as an administrative inspector and was a member of the governor's council.
He was also chairman of the finance committee and the pardons committee.
As a full-time elected official, Coolidge discontinued his law practice in 1916, though his family continued to live in Northampton.
McCall and Coolidge were both reelected in 1916 and in 1917. When McCall decided that he would not stand for a fourth term, Coolidge announced his intention to run for governor.

Coolidge was unopposed for the Republican nomination for ___E:governor of Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Massachusetts)___ in ___E:1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1918_Massachusetts_gubernatorial_election)___ .

He and his running mate, ___E:Channing Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Cox)___ , a Boston lawyer and Speaker of the ___E:Massachusetts House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_House_of_Representatives)___ , ran on the previous administration's record: ___E:fiscal conservatism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_conservatism)___ , a vague opposition to ___E:Prohibition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States)___ , support for women's suffrage, and support for American involvement in ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ .
The issue of the war proved divisive, especially among ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_American)___ and ___E:German Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Americans)___ .

Coolidge was elected by a margin of 16,773 votes over his opponent, ___E:Richard H. Long U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_H._Long)___ , in the smallest margin of victory of any of his statewide campaigns.

In 1919, in reaction to a plan of the policemen of the ___E:Boston Police Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Police_Department)___ to register with a ___E:union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union)___ , Police Commissioner ___E:Edwin U. Curtis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_U._Curtis)___ announced that such an act would not be tolerated.
In August of that year, the ___E:American Federation of Labor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Labor)___ (AFL) issued a charter to the Boston Police Union.

Curtis declared the union's leaders were guilty of insubordination and would be relieved of duty, but indicated he would cancel their suspension if the union was dissolved by September 4.  The mayor of Boston, ___E:Andrew Peters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_James_Peters)___ , convinced Curtis to delay his action for a few days, but with no results, and Curtis suspended the union leaders on September 8.  The following day, about three-quarters of the policemen in Boston went on strike.  [d]
Tacitly but fully in support of Curtis's position, Coolidge closely monitored the situation but initially deferred to the local authorities.
He anticipated that only a resulting measure of lawlessness could sufficiently prompt the public to understand and appreciate the controlling principle: that a policeman does not strike.

That night and the next, there was sporadic violence and rioting in the city.  Concerned about ___E:sympathy strikes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sympathy_strike)___ by the firemen and others, Peters called up some units of the ___E:Massachusetts National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_National_Guard)___ stationed in the Boston area pursuant to an old and obscure legal authority and relieved Curtis of duty.
Coolidge, sensing the severity of circumstances were then in need of his intervention, conferred with Crane's operative, William Butler, and then acted.
He called up more units of the National Guard, restored Curtis to office, and took personal control of the police force.
Curtis proclaimed that all of the strikers were fired from their jobs, and Coolidge called for a new police force to be recruited.

That night Coolidge received a telegram from AFL leader ___E:Samuel Gompers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Gompers)___ . "Whatever disorder has occurred", Gompers wrote, "is due to Curtis's order in which the right of the policemen has been denied".
Coolidge publicly answered Gompers's telegram, denying any justification whatsoever for the strike—and his response launched him into the national consciousness.

Newspapers nationwide picked up on Coolidge's statement and he became the strike's opponents' newest hero. The nation initially did not know what to make of Coolidge, who had maintained a low profile in the Harding administration.

Many had even expected him to be replaced on the ballot in 1924.  Coolidge believed that those of Harding's men under suspicion were entitled to every presumption of innocence, taking a methodical approach to the scandals, principally the ___E:Teapot Dome scandal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teapot_Dome_scandal)___ , while others clamored for rapid punishment of those they presumed guilty.

The resulting resignations of those involved affirmed this. He personally intervened in demanding the resignation of Attorney General ___E:Harry M. Daugherty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_M._Daugherty)___ after Daugherty refused to cooperate with the investigations.

He then set about to confirm that no loose ends remained in the administration, arranging for a full briefing on the wrongdoing. ___E:Harry A. Slattery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_A._Slattery)___ reviewed the facts with him, ___E:Harlan F. Stone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlan_F._Stone)___ analyzed the legal aspects for him, and Senator ___E:William E. Borah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_E._Borah)___ assessed and presented the political factors.

Former Brigadier General ___E:Charles G. Dawes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_G._Dawes)___ was nominated on the third ballot and accepted.

Bryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_W._Bryan)___ nominated for vice president.

La Follette U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_M._La_Follette)___ , a Republican senator from ___E:Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin)___ , split from the GOP to form a new ___E:Progressive Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Party_(United_States,_1924%E2%80%931934))___ .

During Coolidge's presidency, the United States experienced a period of rapid economic growth known as the " ___E:Roaring Twenties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roaring_Twenties)___ ".

He left the administration's industrial policy in the hands of his activist Secretary of Commerce, ___E:Herbert Hoover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover)___ , who energetically used government auspices to promote business efficiency and develop airlines and radio.

Historian ___E:Robert Sobel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Sobel)___ offers some context for Coolidge's laissez-faire ideology, based on the prevailing understanding of ___E:federalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism)___ during his presidency: "As Governor of Massachusetts, Coolidge supported wages and hours legislation, opposed child labor, imposed economic controls during World War I, favored safety measures in factories, and even worker representation on corporate boards.
Did he support these measures while president?

Congress agreed, and tax rates were reduced in Coolidge's term.
In addition to federal tax cuts, Coolidge proposed reductions in federal expenditures and retiring the ___E:federal debt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_public_debt)___ .

Agriculture Secretary ___E:Henry C. Wallace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cantwell_Wallace)___ and other administration officials favored the bill when it was introduced in 1924, but rising prices convinced many in Congress that the bill was unnecessary, and it was defeated just before the 1924 elections.
